Instead of selecting operators based on individual improvement history (standard ALNS/CMCS), CGSB maintains a dynamic 'Enabling Matrix' $E$. An entry $E_{A,B}$ quantifies the conditional probability that applying operator $B$ immediately after a stagnant application of $A$ yields improvement, specifically testing the non-commutative hypothesis where $P(\text{gain}|A \to B) \neq P(\text{gain}|B \to A)$. The system explicitly executes paired 'probe sequences' $(A, B)$ and $(B, A)$ from identical saved states when local stagnation is detected, updating $E$ only if the asymmetry exceeds a statistical threshold. Selection is then biased toward pairs with high enabling scores rather than single-operator success rates.",
